```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea B carries far less non-software risk for a solo operator. It never touches fan payments or creator payouts. Idea A's own brief lists ongoing PCI, 1099-K, KYC/AML, money-transmitter and sales-tax/VAT exposure, and needs a fintech attorney consult before launch. That is heavy setup inside a 90-day window, and errors carry legal and financial liability.",
    "Switching costs favor B within 90 days. A's brief admits creators face real migration costs for subscribers and payment history, which historically required the founder to bring their own audience. B's brief describes low switching costs, which makes it easier for a newcomer to win a first paying customer.",
    "B's channel economics are better evidenced. B cites a sourced B2B SaaS SEO CAC of $480–942 per customer with a 7-month payback. A cites only a generic $31/lead benchmark and then concedes incumbent SERP dominance likely pushes real cost higher, so A's own brief undercuts its channel number.",
    "B's demand evidence is broader. It cites recurring developer complaints across 2023–2025 plus a named customer testimonial showing businesses pay for this exact fix. A has two r/patreon fee complaints, and one of them names an existing competitor, Ko-fi, as the switching destination. That signals demand already captured by incumbents.",
    "Both markets are saturated, so crowding does not separate them. The difference is buyer type: B sells to technical B2B buyers with budget, at a price anchored to Prerender.io's published tiers. A sells to fee-sensitive creators whose core complaint is price, a pitch competitors already match at 0% (Beamly, Ko-fi Free)."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's central 'Case For' rests on one sourced anecdote: the Spencer Patterson Starter Story case of ~$140K MRR and a $3.5M exit. The brief itself conditions that success on the founder already owning a niche audience, which it says most solo builders lack on day one. So the only proof the wedge works does not transfer to the stated founder profile.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B has real gaps. Its Reddit demand quotes carry subreddit and year but no URLs. The full competitor list it references is not included; only Prerender.io's pricing is sourced. The community-outreach channel cost is marked [unsourced] and counts as missing. Its own sourced Google guidance labels prerendering a workaround and points toward SSR frameworks, implying a shrinking market. These weaknesses matter more for long-term viability than for landing a first paying customer in 90 days. A's regulatory burden and audience dependency are more direct obstacles to that goal."
}
```
